correctness.rationale: For a nondegenerate rank-one-square algebra, the multiplier form is nondegenerate and natural bases are exactly orthogonal bases. Each admissible nonzero diagonal tuple has an orthogonal-group torsor of presentations; Witt transitivity equidistributes the nonzero fixed-norm distinguished vector. For k<n, one free diagonal coefficient makes the discriminant condition uniform; for k=n, the remaining character χ(product a_i) gives exactly δG_n(c). Additive orthogonality and quadratic Gauss sums evaluate A and G for all odd prime powers. The all-k normalization is exact. Explicit comparison of A_n and |G_n| yields the three q=3 full-support exclusions. A standalone executable enumerator checked 12 (field,n) cases, 128 feasible parameter types, and 4 direct natural-basis examples over prime fields. Finite enumeration is auxiliary; the general proof does not depend on it.

value.rationale: The October 2026 evolution-algebra survey specifically asks for graph information that can survive changes of natural basis, including natural classes. For a nonperfect, nondegenerate rank-one-square algebra, the directed graph can genuinely change with the natural basis; the theorem gives not just existence but a complete finite-field probability vector and an exact count of bases for each graph type in all dimensions, plus the sharp q=3 full-support exceptions. This is a natural complete invariant for an infinite algebra family, rather than a small finite example or routine substitution. The modest scope (only rank-one squares and odd fields) is explicit.
